eligibility_note: Own panel estimation (PCSE/FGLS); exposure is ICT/broadband/mobile/internet; 10 ASEAN economies plus explicit income-group comparison; outcome is GDP per capita (output family 1). Eligible.

sample_corrections.years: 1995-2020 confirmed ('annual observations from 1995 to 2020'); the '1000 observations over 10 years' statement is internally inconsistent with 10 economies x 26 years (max 260) and should not be used as N

results.correction: Numbers correct, but direction 'mixed' is wrong: both PCSE (0.090, p=0.052) and FGLS (0.317, p=0.000) are positive; PCSE is only borderline significant. Direction should be positive.

results.quote: lnRFLC 0.923 (T11), 0.5181 (T8), 1.0492 (T9), 0.3042 0.690 (T10); Model 4 PCSE. Variable is a fee, not remittances; not an ICT exposure per se

heterogeneity.quote: MBP shows strong positive effects in Models 3-4 (p < 0.01) (high-income paragraph); Tables 8-10 rows lnMBP
IUI 0.0060 (T8), -0.0017 (T9), -0.0009 p=0.054 (T10); 'its impact may not be linear. Beyond a certain threshold' (6.1.1) - no nonlinear term in tables

income_group_note: High/upper-middle/lower-middle coefficients in the record match Tables 8-10 PCSE Model 4 (e.g. lnMBP 0.1895, -0.1174, -0.0645; lnMCSMI -0.18344, 0.1061, 0.1102). No low-income economy.

risk_of_bias.confounding_reverse_causation: agree - static regressions, no instrument or lags; authors concede endogeneity and call results 'short-run associations'; price variables deflated by GDP per capita on the right-hand side.
risk_of_bias.exposure_measurement: agree - variable labels mismatch (RFLC called remittances, FTSFLI fintech, FBPH/MBP described as rates but reported as large counts) and logging of IUI/IRPTR is unclear.
risk_of_bias.selection_of_countries_years: too_harsh - the ASEAN-10 panel is the full region rather than a selected sample; the real weaknesses are 2-economy subgroups and an inconsistent observation count ('1000 observations'), which fit moderate.
risk_of_bias.outcome_measurement: agree - World Bank GDP per capita in logs is a standard outcome, though text mislabels it as growth.
risk_of_bias.specification: agree - I(1) variables regressed in levels without cointegration, R-squared near 1.000, no fixed effects reported, no preferred specification.
risk_of_bias.selective_reporting: agree - all four models and both estimators are printed, but narrative cites 'b = 0.046, p = 0.001' for FBPH, which matches no Table 11 entry (0.060, p=0.009).
risk_of_bias.why: Serious overall: causal wording with no strategy for reverse causation and spurious-regression risk from non-cointegrated I(1) levels, plus mislabelled exposure variables.

problems: Only one error: result 4 direction labelled mixed though both estimators are positive. Record's 'Table 7 sums imply about 144 country-years' is the extractor's own inference and not checked. Source mislabels (RFLC as remittances, FTSFLI as fintech) are real, as the record says.
